name: opening_range_breakout_5s_3
author: adapted from AI_Quant
thesis: This strategy uses the Opening Range Breakout (ORB): it enters when price breaks the high/low of the first 15-minutes of trading【10†L48-L56】. The idea is early volatility (reflecting overnight news and institutional orders) sets a directional bias, so breaking out signals continuation【10†L137-L145】. It persists because many traders wait passively, underreacting to the 'first hour' signal, and the OR levels are self-fulfilling reference points.
mechanism: Consolidation periods accumulate resting orders above resistance and below support. A breakout triggers these resting orders as stop-losses and breakout entries fire simultaneously. The resulting order flow imbalance overwhelms the resting liquidity, and market makers widen spreads in the breakout direction, accelerating the move.
weaknesses: High risk of false breakouts or breakout failures (whipsaws)
Very sensitive to exact timeframe of opening range (overfitting risk)
Strategy assumes sufficient volatility; may fail on calm days
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
